title: Image preview
description: Render a real-time preview of the selected image in the terminal. Support common image formats. Display updates as the selection changes in the file list.

title: ANSI terminal graphics rendering
description: Render image previews using ANSI terminal graphics so images display inline in the terminal.

title: Graphical protocol support (kitty, iTerm2)
description: Support the kitty and iTerm2 graphical converter protocols for higher-fidelity inline images. Works on Ghostty and iTerm2 terminals.

title: Picture-to-text converters (chafa, jp2a)
description: Provide multiple picture-to-text converters: chafa and jp2a. Each converter has its own configurable options (chafa format/colors; jp2a colors/invert/dither/chars; graphical filter_type/max_dimension/auto_resize).

title: Switch converters with TAB
description: Cycle between the available converters at runtime by pressing TAB, re-rendering the current preview with the newly selected converter.

title: Caching of rendered images
description: Cache rendered image output for performance so revisiting a file does not re-render from scratch.

title: Text file preview
description: Preview text files in addition to images. Scroll a selected text file up/down with u / space.

title: File browser navigation
description: Browse the filesystem with a scrollable file list. Navigate with arrow keys or vim-style j/k, Page Up/Down (or Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B) to jump a page, f/b to jump 10 files, Home/End to list ends.

title: Directory traversal
description: Enter a directory with Enter and go to the parent directory with Backspace.

title: Scrollable file lists
description: Handle directories with many files via a scrollable list that keeps the selection visible.

title: Re-read file list (r)
description: Press r to re-read the file list, preview and rating while keeping the current selection.

title: Open in system file browser (o)
description: Press o to open the current location in the system file-system browser, if one is available.

title: Slideshow mode
description: Start a slideshow with space; advance with arrow keys or j/k. Configurable delay between slides (slideshow_delay_ms). Optional transitions (only with the jp2a converter), with configurable effect and frame duration.

title: Star ratings
description: Rate the selected file 0-5 (keys 1-5, 0 clears, * = five). The rating shows as a star and number in the file list.

title: XMP sidecar storage
description: Store ratings as XMP sidecar files holding the standard xmp:Rating property, interoperable with darktable, digiKam, RawTherapee, Adobe Bridge and Lightroom, syncing via Dropbox/rsync and surviving a move to another machine.

title: Sidecar naming conventions
description: Read both appended (photo.jpg.xmp) and replaced (photo.xmp) sidecar conventions. Write whichever a folder already uses, else the appended form. Hide sidecars whose image is present; keep visible an orphaned sidecar so it can be deleted.

title: Non-destructive sidecar updates
description: Never overwrite an existing sidecar; only update xmp:Rating and xmp:MetadataDate, leaving all other metadata (e.g. darktable edit history) untouched.

title: Private rating fallback
description: When sidecars are declined for a folder, keep ratings privately in ptui state.json. stars.sidecars config of ask (default, prompt once per folder) / always / never controls behavior.

title: Rating follows file operations
description: Deleting a file deletes its sidecar; copying/moving a file carries its sidecar along. Private ratings follow a copy or move the same way.

title: Sort file list
description: Sort by date (d: newest/oldest), name (n: A-Z/Z-A), or rating (s: best-first/unrated-first). Repeated press of a sort key reverses order; files sharing a key are ordered by name.

title: File operations
description: Act on the selected file from within the browser.

title: Delete file (x)
description: Delete the selected file with x (also removes its sidecar).

title: Copy / move file (c / m)
description: Copy (c) or move (m) the selected file to a destination chosen from a numbered shortcut list (last-used, then standard folders: home, desktop, downloads, documents, pictures, projects). Final entry switches to free-text path entry (~ expanded, relative paths resolved against the browsed folder; Ctrl+U clears, Esc returns to list). Overwrite of a same-named file requires y confirmation. Last destination remembered in state.json.

title: Save picture to ASCII (i)
description: Save the current picture as ASCII art with i.

title: Multilingual support
description: Provide UI in multiple locales: English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Chinese. Locale set via the locale config key.

title: Dynamic window resizing
description: Resize the preview window with [ and ] keys, and adapt automatically when the terminal size changes.

title: Help and quit controls
description: Show help with ?. Quit from anywhere with q / Esc / Ctrl+C, including while a dialog is open.

title: Configuration file
description: Auto-create a JSON config at ~/.config/ptui/ptui.json (Linux) or $HOME/Library/Application Support/ptui/ptui.json (Mac), seeded from docs/example.config.ptui.json defaults.

title: Partial config with defaults
description: Only keys present in the file take effect; everything missing uses its default, so a short config is valid.

title: Live config reload
description: Edits to the config refresh in the running app automatically.

title: Config parse-error resilience
description: If the config cannot be parsed, leave the file untouched, run on defaults for that session, and report the problem (line and column) in the messages pane, so a stray comma never costs the file.

title: Runtime requirements
description: Depend on chafa (ANSI/terminal output) and ImageMagick (identify, for image dimensions). jp2a optional (only when the jp2a converter is selected). nasm only needed when building with the fast-jpeg feature.

title: Installation channels
description: Installable from source on Arch Linux and Mac (cargo build --features fast-jpeg --release; cargo install --locked --path .), from the AUR (ptui-bin), and from Homebrew (narbs/homebrew-tap/narbs-ptui).
